My case against rushing a name is this:

1. Elsa recorded silence as the bazaar’s first fact; Inigo listed ten living seats and zero shutters overnight—both are exact and undisputed.
2. Gandalf’s roll call and Elsa’s ledger opening show no merchant has yet claimed a role or brought evidence of wrongdoing.

What evidence do Gandalf, Inigo, and Elsa each bring that a Family member walks among us tonight?

Hermione: Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo — you keep the roster and the silence, yet none of you answer the plain question put twice: where is the quote or observed act that shows wrongdoing?

Sherlock, you called for facts; I ask you now: what concrete evidence do you weigh today? Point to the merchant whose words or silence you treat as proof.

Neo, Ripley, Batman, Morpheus — you pressed the same call; the ledger waits for your evidence.

The bazaar’s only truth so far is silence counted exactly.

Hermione: Sherlock, Neo, Ripley, Elsa, Batman, Gandalf — you all pressed Morpheus to name the concrete quote or act that steered suspicion, yet none of you have produced one yourselves.

Neo called Sherlock’s call “louder than the facts themselves.” The bazaar’s only truth remains the roster and the graveyard: ten names, zero departures, zero role reveals.

Therefore I ask each of you plainly: which merchant’s own words or observed action do you weigh as proof tonight? The ledger is ready for your answer.

My case against Sherlock stands on two exhibits:
1. Sherlock writes Morpheus “refuse[s] to quote the line that steered your suspicion” (21:01:11Z) yet Sherlock himself has not quoted any line or act steering suspicion toward any merchant.
2. Sherlock now repeats the same accusation (21:02:16Z) while offering zero ledger-worthy facts.

The bazaar’s only verifiable truths: ten merchants, zero shutters overnight, zero role reveals. Until Sherlock supplies a merchant’s own quoted words or an observed act, his accusation is noise.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo—your silence remains clean; no mouth has quoted you toward suspicion. The ledger waits for Sherlock’s evidence.

Hermione: Sherlock, Neo, Ripley, Elsa, Batman, Morpheus — six voices now chant the same empty call: “quote the line.” Yet none of you has supplied one. Sherlock twice repeats Morpheus “refuses to quote the line that steered suspicion” while Sherlock himself names no merchant whose words he weighs. Neo echoes Sherlock’s exact call; Ripley counts nine demands yet offers none; Elsa and Batman do the same. The bazaar’s only ledger is the roster and the graveyard: ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals. The compact asks for plain speech.

Sherlock, your second call for Morpheus to “quote the line that steered suspicion” still hangs empty: you named none of your own. Neo, Ripley, Elsa, Batman, Hermione — you five joined the same chant tonight, yet none of you supply a quoted line or observed act. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo — your silence stays clean; no mouth has quoted you toward suspicion. The bazaar’s only verifiable facts remain the roster and the graveyard: ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals. Until the loudest accusers name the merchant whose own quoted words they lean on, we trade in open air.

Hermione: Sherlock, your chorus now numbers seven voices chanting the same empty cadence—Neo, Ripley, Elsa, Batman, Morpheus, Gandalf, yourself—yet none supply the merchant whose quoted words you lean on. Yoda twice called Morpheus’s pivot plain; Hermione accused Sherlock on paper yet offered none herself. The bazaar’s compact is not a chorus—it is the single merchant whose own quoted words you weigh. Name that merchant now or own the absence; the record will not wait for echoes.

Hermione to Sherlock, Neo, Ripley, Elsa, Batman, Gandalf, Morpheus: seven voices now chant the same refrain—“name the merchant whose quoted words you weigh”—yet every voice in that chorus withholds the merchant they claim to lean on. Sherlock twice wrote Morpheus “refuses to quote the line that steered suspicion,” yet Sherlock himself has not quoted a single ledger-worthy line steering suspicion toward any merchant tonight. The roster and graveyard still read ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals. The compact rewards plain speech, not volume; point to the merchant or admit the absence before the bell cuts the square short.
